The Engine Started
Bitcoin broke through the resistance in the $75,500 range that had been holding the price back for a week, posting the highest high of this recovery cycle at
. The volume of 25,885 BTC traded was
48% above the 7-day average
, confirming that the move has real market participation.

On the weekly timeframe, the price remains below the 50 and 100-week EMAs (around $86,700 and $82,600, respectively), which keeps the medium-term structure bearish. However, the cumulative +18.8% recovery from the $65,000 bottom in March and four consecutive weeks of higher closes show that buyers have regained control in the short term.

If the Momentum Continues
The trigger to confirm the bullish scenario is a daily close above

with sustained volume above 20,000 BTC. The first target sits in the $82,600 range, where the 100-week EMA lies — the first relevant weekly moving average above the current price. The secondary target would be near $86,700 (50-week EMA), a level that, if reclaimed, would shift the weekly structure back to bullish.

The fuel for this rally is lined up: 62.5% of futures accounts are short with a negative funding rate of -0.0081%. This creates potential for a quick reversal through short liquidations above $78,300. Bitcoin rose only 2.90% while the NASDAQ advanced 6.84%, creating room for a convergence move over the next 24 to 48 hours.
The Fear & Greed Index left "Extreme Fear" for the first time in over a week, posting
(Fear). Price rising while sentiment remains fearful is historically a sign of strength — most traders haven't positioned for the upside yet.
If the Strength Fades
The bearish trigger is a daily close below
, a support tested three consecutive times between April 14 and 16 that coincides with the weekly low from March 17. Losing this level would open the path to the 200-week EMA in the
range, which serves as a cycle-bottom indicator. The secondary target would be
, the macro bottom from late March.
The invalidation of this scenario would come with a weekly close above $78,333 accompanied by rising volume and the funding rate flipping positive. The daily RSI at
is the main short-term warning signal — above 70 since early April and still climbing, which signals strong momentum but also warns of possible exhaustion.
On the Radar Tomorrow
The decisive level is

: a close above it could trigger a wave of short liquidations. A rejection with weak volume puts the $73,300 support back in the spotlight. On the macro front, the weak dollar (DXY at 98.2) and the strong rally in U.S. equities (S&P 500
) keep the environment favorable for risk assets.
